verdicts.why: No finding is about an allocation sized by an untrusted length field. The closest, F02, does concern parsing of table/array payloads but its claimed exploit is premature loop exit because InputStream.available() may return 0 - a framing/desync issue, not a buffer allocated from a declared length before the payload is known to exist. F01 is a timestamp arithmetic overflow with no allocation involved.

No finding concerns recursion depth. F02 touches the same readTable/readArray loops but only to argue that available() can end them too early; it never says the routines call each other in an uncounted cycle whose depth follows input nesting. Recursion, nesting depth, and StackOverflowError are absent from both findings.
